chapter: Arrival and the Pete Lala photograph
title: The lost Excelsior band picture, the 1915 date and the clarinet
summary: They discuss the misplaced Excelsior band photo and the 1915 date on the Pete Lala picture, the five-piece lineup, and copying the photo.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: I wonder where we could find that, I don't know, we lost the picture of the old Excelsior band. It was around here and I don't know what happened to it.
I don't know, I had to look for it.

Well, it's been misplaced a long time. I don't know what happened. I guess it was thrown away. A whole lot of stuff we, well, it didn't have no place. We had a big shed there. We had to tear it down and have a string, you see, and a kennel in there. That's too bad, William Gonzalo. You know, it's wonderful stuff to have. It was, we had some, we had a nice library too, music.
Oh, yeah. They just couldn't keep it all. They had no place to keep it. The date on this picture says February 28th, 1915. Is that right, I guess? That's about it. Let's see.
My grandfather must have put that in. He was, he, now they dig pictures. But that's my granddaddy's handwriting. Oh, right there, really?
And you see, and he's got the names or something back in here now. I don't know, my daddy, February, he got dates back in it, so.
What was the name of that band? Do you know, did they have a name for it?

Well, all I know is Pete Lawler's band. They work at the cabaret. Did that happen? The British Christian. What was the name of the band, one of the Pete Lawler's band, wasn't it? That's all right. Sure, sure. Yeah, we're at the cabaret, you know what I mean. Yeah, the cabaret's over at the band. They're hard to different men, you see? Yeah.
I, uh, the bass on violin, and me on the carinet, boy, Chris on the piano, and the drums. All right. And bass. Yeah, you had no bass. You had a bass in that.
Five, five pieces. Didn't have no bass regular, but in that picture you got a bass. That ball game or something y'all played. Y'all used to play that ball game, do you know? Mm-hmm.

This picture's taken outdoors by a big fence. It looks like the clarinet is a little bit short. Did you play a B flat or a C clarinet? B flat clarinet. B flat, I guess it's B flat then. You were a big man though, so it looked small in your hand. Uh-huh, sure.
You only worked 12 pounds at the time.
You been eating up, buddy. You kind of up there now with your weight.
Yeah, you look almost as heavy as Percy here. Oh, he was a big man.
Oh, yes, he was. Yeah. Put it weight about 12 pounds.

Yes, maybe we could make a copy of this by making another photograph of this with a new negative, then we could get a new print of it, too. You could, eh? Mm-hmm. And they have a way of photographing the photograph. Yeah. And reproducing it. It won't be too clear, but at least it'll show it.
